name: City Council Meeting - Mar 26, 2024
agenda_text:
TORRANCE CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
  MARCH 26, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING
  5:00 P.M. - CLOSED SESSION
  6:30 P.M. - REGULAR BUSINESS BEGINS
  IN COUNCIL CHAMBER AT 3031 TORRANCE BL.

  CITY COUNCIL MAY TAKE ACTION ON ANY ITEM LISTED ON THE AGENDA

Revised City Council Agenda 03-26-2024

*Denotes the item was modified after posting of the agenda.

OPENING CEREMONIES

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  ROLL CALL
  : Councilmembers Griffiths, Kaji, Kalani, Lewis, Mattucci, Sheikh, and Mayor Chen

14.  CLOSED SESSION

  14A. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION (California
  Government Code §54956.9(d)(1)):
  1)  Jose Alberto Hilario Hernandez v. City of Torrance, et al. LASC Case No.
  22TRCV01593
  2)  Eric Hickman v. City of Torrance LASC Case No. 19STCV37386
  3)  Glen Allen v. City of Torrance, et al. LASC Case No. 24LBCV00305
  4)  Junior Moananu v. Torrance Police Department, et al. LASC Case No. 24TRCV00461
  14A - STAFF REPORT

  14B. PUBLIC EMPLOYEE DISCIPLINE/DISMISSAL/RELEASE (California Government
  Code §54957):

  14C. PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION (California Government Code
  §54957(b)(1)): Title: City Attorney

  14D. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (California Government Code
  §54957.6): Agency Negotiator: Aram Chaparyan Employee
  Organization/Association:
  1. Certain Full-Time Salaried and Hourly Employees
  2. Certain Part-Time Hourly Employees
  3. Crossing Guards
  4. Elected Officials
  5. Engineers and Torrance Fiscal Employees Association
  6. Executive & Management Employees
  7. Police & Fire Trainees

  10. Fire Safety Management
  11. Torrance Fire Fighters Association
  12. Torrance Library Employees Association
  13. Torrance Municipal Employees/AFSCME Local 1117 AFL-CIO
  14. Torrance Police Commanders Association (TPCA)
  15. Torrance Police Officers Association
  16. Torrance Professional Parks & Recreation Employees Organization
  17. Torrance Professional & Supervisory Association
  18. Torrance Recurrent Recreational Employees Organization
  19. City Treasurer
   20. City Clerk
  21. City Attorney
  22. City Manager

  14E. REAL PROPERTY – CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR
  (California Government Code §54956.8):
  1)  Property: 3481 Airport Drive, #200, Torrance, CA 90505 Agency Negotiator: Aram
  Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and Torrance Flite Park, LLC Under
  Negotiation: Price and terms and conditions of lease
  2)  Property: 1345 Post Avenue, Torrance, CA 90501 Agency Negotiator: Aram Chaparyan
  Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and Torrance Historical Society Under Negotiation:
  Price and terms and conditions of lease
  3)  Property: 17498 Hawthorne Boulevard, Torrance, CA 90504 Agency Negotiator: Aram
  Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and Rosalinde and Arthur Gilbert
  Foundation (Matthews Real Estate Investment Services, Inc) Under Negotiation: Price
  and terms and conditions of lease
  4)  Property: 2600 Skypark Drive, Torrance, CA 90505 Agency Negotiator: Aram
  Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and Hi-Shear Corporation Under
  Negotiation: Price and terms and conditions of lease

RECESSED TO CLOSED SESSION - Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9 (d)(1)

RECONVENED IN PUBLIC SESSION

2.  FLAG SALUTE: Councilmember Lewis NON-SECTARIAN INVOCATION:
  Councilmember Mattucci

3.  REPORT OF THE CITY CLERK ON THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA The agenda was
  posted on the Public Notice Board at 3031 Torrance Bl. and on the City’s Website on
  Tuesday, March 19, 2024 /s/ Rebecca Poirier
  3 - Affidavit

MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READING OF RESOLUTIONS AND ORDINANCES AFTER
NUMBER & TITLE – See Council Rules of Order Section 2.11 (Resolution 2006-65)

4.  ANNOUNCEMENT OF WITHDRAWN, DEFERRED, AND/OR SUPPLEMENTAL ITEMS

5.  COUNCIL COMMITTEE MEETINGS AND ANNOUNCEMENTS

6.  COMMUNITY MATTERS – None Scheduled.

7.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS #1 (Limited up to a 15-minute period) This portion of the
  meeting is reserved for comment on items under the Consent Calendar or items that
  are not on the agenda. Under the Ralph M. Brown Act, City Council cannot act on
  items raised during public comment but may respond briefly to statements made or
  questions posed; request clarification; or refer the item to staff. Speakers under Orals
  are limited to either Oral Communications #1 or Oral Communications #2 and no
  longer than 1 minute per speaker. If presenting handout material to Council, please
  provide 11 copies to the City Clerk before speaking.
  PUBLIC COMMENT
  LATE PUBLIC COMMENT RECIEVED AFTER 5:30 P.M. ON 3/25/24 AND PRIOR TO
  ADJOURMENT AT 1:52 A.M. ON 3/27/24

8.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  Matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion and one
  vote. There will be no separate discussion of these items. If discussion is desired, that item will be removed by
  a Councilmember from the Consent Calendar and considered separately..

  8A. City Clerk – Approve City Council Minutes. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Clerk that City Council approve the City Council minutes of
  February 27, 2024.

  8B. Community Development – Approve Final Parcel Map No. 83607, Accept
   Additional Street Easements, Abandon Two Public Utility and Planting
  Easements, and Determine that Approval of Final Parcel Map No. 83607 is
  Categorically Exempt from California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Pursuant to Section 15268(b) of the CEQA Guidelines. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Development Director that City Council:
  1) Approve Final Parcel Map No. 83607; and
  2) Accept additional street and highway easements at the following locations:
  3) Abandon two unneeded Public Utility and Planting easements along the north side of
  195th Street; and
  4) Determine that approval of Final Parcel Map No. 83607 is categorically exempt from
  the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15268(b) of the
  CEQA Guidelines.
  8B - STAFF REPORT

  8D. Civil Service Commission and Human Resources – Approve Proposed Class
  Specification for Fire Prevention Supervisor. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Civil Service Commission and Human Resources Director that City
  Council approve the proposed class specification for Fire Prevention Supervisor.
  8D - STAFF REPORT

  8E.  Civil Service Commission and Human Resources – Approve Revised Class
  Specification for Human Resources Technician. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Civil Service Commission and Human Resources Director that City
  Council approve the revised class specification for Human Resources Technician.
  8E - STAFF REPORT

  8C. Community Development – Accept and File 2023 Housing Element Annual
  Progress Report and Authorize Submission to California Department of Housing
  and Community Development and Governor’s Office of Planning and Research.
  Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Development Director that City Council:
  1) Accept and file the 2023 Housing Element Annual Progress Report; and
  2) Authorize staff to submit the 2023 Housing Element Annual Progress Report to the
  California Department of Housing and Community Development; and
  3) Authorize staff to submit the 2023 Housing Element Annual Progress Report to the
  Governor’s Office of Planning and Research.
  8C - STAFF REPORT

RECESS

RECONVENE

8.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  Matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion and one
  vote. There will be no separate discussion of these items. If discussion is desired, that item will be removed by
  a Councilmember from the Consent Calendar and considered separately..

9.  ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS

  9A. City Manager – Appropriate Funds and Award Contract Services Agreement for
  Audio Visual & Control System Upgrades. Expenditure: Not-to-Exceed
  $578,092.60 (Non-General Fund).
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1) Appropriate $237,092.60 from the Public, Educational, and Governmental Access
  Fund’s fund balance to the Public, Educational, and Governmental Access Fund’s fiscal
  year 2023-24 operating budget; and
  2) Appropriate $578,092.60 from the Public, Educational, and Governmental Access
  Fund’s fiscal year 2023-24 operating budget to Facility, Equipment, and Automation
  Plan (FEAP) 950 – City Council TV Production Control Room, Cameras, Robotics
  project; and
  3) Award a contract services agreement to Triton Technology Solutions, Inc. of San Juan
  Capistrano, CA (RFP B2023-44) for an amount not-to-exceed $578,092.60 to provide
  audio visual and control system upgrades in the LeRoy J. Jackson Council Chamber
  for a one-year period beginning March 26, 2024, and ending March 25, 2025.
   9A - STAFF REPORT

  9B. City Manager – Approve One-Time Exemption to Torrance Municipal Code (TMC)
  Section 46.5.3b Regarding Hours for Amplified Sound and Approve Amplified
  Sound Permit for Islamic Center of South Bay Event at Charles H. Wilson Park.
  Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1) Approve a one-time exemption to Torrance Municipal Code (TMC) section 46.5.3b
  regarding hours for Amplified Sound; and
  2) Approve an Amplified Sound Permit for the Islamic Center of South Bay-Lomita for
  prayer services to be held on April 10, 2024 at Charles H. Wilson Park, 2200 Crenshaw
  Boulevard.
  9B - STAFF REPORT

  9C. City Manager – Review and Concur with Provisions of the Downtown Torrance
  Business Improvement District Management District (BID) Plan, Provide
  Direction on Assessment Obligations, and Authorize City Manager to Submit
  Affirmative Petitions for Establishment of Downtown Torrance Business
  Improvement District. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1) Review and concur with the provisions of the Downtown Torrance Business
  Improvement District (BID) Management District Plan; and
  2) Provide direction on assessment obligations for City owned properties; and
  3) Authorize the City Manager to submit affirmative petitions supporting the establishment
  of a Downtown Torrance Business Improvement District.
  9C - STAFF REPORT
  LATE PUBLIC COMMENT

  9D. City Attorney – Approve Seventh Amendment to Fee Agreement for Legal
  Services. Expenditure: $1,758,371.70 (General Fund).
  Recommendation of the City Attorney that City Council approve a seventh amendment to
  the fee agreement with law firm Rutan & Tucker, LLP of Costa Mesa, CA (C2020-038) in the
  amount of $1,758,371.70, for a new not-to-exceed amount of $7,973,371.70, to cover costs
  and provide legal services relating to the 2020 Los Angeles Regional Water Quality Control
  Board Order/Hi-Shear litigation.
  9D - STAFF REPORT

  9E.  City Manager and Communications and Information Technology – Receive
  Update and Provide Direction on Potential Installation of Live Webcam in
  Torrance. Expenditure: None. In response to an oral request by Councilmember
  Aurelio Mattucci, it is the recommendation of the City Manager and
  Communications and Information Technology Director that City Council receive
  an update and provide direction on the potential installation of a live webcam in
  Torrance as a means of promoting the City in a visual medium.
  9E - STAFF REPORT

*The following item was modified on Thursday, March 21, 2024.

  9F.  City Manager – Adopt RESOLUTIONS Authorizing Grant of Easement and
  Settlement and Release Agreement for Portions of City-Owned Vacant
  Properties. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1) Adopt findings that portions of city-owned vacant properties (7532-011-900 and 7532-
  011-901) are exempt surplus land under the California Surplus Land Act as defined by
  California Government Code, Section 54221; and
  2) Adopt a RESOLUTION authorizing and directing the Mayor to execute and the City
  Clerk to attest to grant of easement entitled Easement Agreement with Covenants,
  Conditions, and Restrictions for portions of city-owned vacant properties (7532-011-900
  and 7532-011-901); and
  3) Adopt a RESOLUTION authorizing and directing the Mayor to execute and the City
  Clerk to attest to a Settlement and Release Agreement between the City of Torrance
  and the property owners of 4805 Paseo de las Tortugas to cure an encroachment
  dispute.
   9F - STAFF REPORT

  9G. City Clerk – Adopt ORDINANCE Amending the Torrance Municipal Code
  Regarding Changes to Commission Appointments and Terms, and Filling of
  Vacancies and Determine California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Exemption and Discuss and Provide Direction Regarding Commission Meeting
  Times and Combining or Disbanding Commissions. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Clerk that City Council:
  1) Discuss and consider amending the Torrance Municipal Code to consider changes to
  Commission appointments and terms of members and filling of vacancies; and
  2) Adopt an ORDINANCE amending Torrance Municipal Code Sections 13.1.2, 13.2.2,
  13.3.2, 13.4.2, 13.5.2, 13.9.2, 13.10.2, 13.11.2, 13.15.2, 13.16.2, 13.18.2, 13.20.020
  and 13.21.030 all titled “Appointment and Terms of Members” and Sections 13.1.3,
  13.2.3, 13.3.3, 13.5.3, 13.9.3, 13.15.3, 13.16.3, 13.18.3, 13.20.030 and 13.21.040 all
  titled “Filling of Vacancies; and
  3) Determine the project is exempt from California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to Sections 15378 and 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines; and
  4) Approve an Ordinance Summary for publication; and
  5) Discuss and provide direction regarding meeting times and combining or disbanding
  Commissions.
  9G - STAFF REPORT
  9G - SUPPLEMENTAL

  9H. City Manager, General Services, and Public Works - Receive Update and Provide
  Direction on Potential Installation of New Electronic Message Board.
  Expenditure: None.
  In response to an oral request by Councilmember Mike Griffiths with City Council
  concurrence, it is the recommendation of the City Manager, General Services Director, and
  Public Works Director that City Council receive an update and provide direction on the
  potential installation of a new electronic message board near the southwest corner of
  Hawthorne Boulevard and Pacific Coast Highway intersection.
  9H - STAFF REPORT

RECESS

RECONVENE

10.  HEARINGS

  10A. Community Development – Conduct Public Hearing on Land Use Study 24-00002
  Regarding Proposed Amendments to Torrance Municipal Code Pertaining to
  Electronic/Digital Billboards, Determine California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) Exemption, and Adopt ORDINANCE Amending Torrance Municipal Code.
  Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Development Director that City Council:
  1) Conduct a public hearing on Land Use Study 24-00002 regarding proposed
  amendments to the Torrance Municipal Code pertaining to Electronic/Digital Billboards;
  and
  2) Determine that the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines; and
  3) Adopt an ORDINANCE amending Torrance Municipal Code Section 911.6.100 entitled
  “Prohibited Signs” of Chapter 11, Article 6, Division 9; repealing Article 10 entitled
  “Enforcement” of Chapter 11, Division 9; adding Article 10 entitled “Electronic/Digital
  Billboards” to Chapter 11, Division 9; adding Article 11 entitled “Enforcement” to
  Chapter 11, Division 9; and
  4) Approve an Ordinance Summary for publication.
  10A - STAFF REPORT
  10A - STAFF PRESENTATION
  10A - SUPPLEMENTAL

11.  AGENCY AGENDAS – None Scheduled.

12.  2ND READING ORDINANCES
   12A. Second and Final reading of ORDINANCE NO. 3931 amending Section 91.37.3(a)
  of Chapter 1 of Article 37 of Division 9 of the Torrance Municipal Code to regulate
  the approval process and placement of pickleball courts in the P-U (Public Use)
  Zone and approve an Ordinance Summary for publication.
  12A - STAFF REPORT
  12A - SUPPLEMENTAL

13.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS #2 (Limited up to a 15-minute period) Council Order –
  Mattucci, Sheikh, Griffiths, Kaji, Kalani, Lewis and Mayor Chen This portion of the
  meeting is reserved for comments on items not on the agenda. Under the Ralph M.
  Brown Act, City Council cannot act on items raised during public comment but may
  respond briefly to statements made or questions posed; request clarification; or refer
  the item to staff. Speakers under Orals are limited to either Oral Communications #1
  or Oral Communications #2 and no longer than 1 minute per speaker. If presenting
  handout material to Council, please provide 11 copies to the City Clerk before
  speaking.

RECONVENE

RECONVENE

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  15A. Adjournment of City Council meeting to Tuesday, April 9, 2024, at 5:00 p.m. for
  closed session, with regular business commencing at 6:30 p.m. in the Leroy J.
  Jackson Council Chamber. Tuesday, April 2, 2024, is a Council Dark Night.
  15A - STAFF REPORT
